claims.text: The widget command line entry point parses its arguments, loads one widget by name, prints its description and returns exit code 0.

cite.quote:
def main(argv=None):
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    widget = load(args.command or "default")
    print(Widget.describe(widget))
    return 0

claims.text: The wheel ships exactly one package, widget, while pytest is pointed at tests, which is why the test files sit outside the declared package.
One import in this repo has no file behind it: default_settings imports widget.config from inside the function body, so the module itself still imports cleanly.

cite.quote:
from widget.config import SETTINGS

    return SETTINGS

claims.text: The loader raises KeyError when it is handed a name that is not in SIZES, so an unknown widget name fails fast instead of being constructed.
Despite the pyproject and the console script, this is not an application anyone runs: its own docstrings describe the layout as a fixture built to exercise a tool that reads repositories.
